subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a public task notify default config surface, and should that surface be one global default or a per-runtime policy map for ACP, subagent, cron, CLI, and Task Flow records?
rationale: The source gap is real, but repository policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and the choice affects channel message volume and suppression semantics across several open issues.

options.title: Add per-runtime defaults
options.body: Add an additive `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map that defaults to current behavior and lets maintainers preserve cron/CLI/media silence while users tune ACP and subagent notifications.

options.title: Add one global default
options.body: Expose a smaller single default that is easier to document but risks flattening today’s runtime-specific behavior unless exceptions are hardcoded.

options.title: Defer to narrower policies
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers resolve Discord/Codex/ACP-specific visibility and flood-control issues before adding a cross-runtime config surface.

recommendation.title: Add per-runtime defaults
recommendation.body: Add an additive `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map that defaults to current behavior and lets maintainers preserve cron/CLI/media silence while users tune ACP and subagent notifications.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the clearest recent history on the shared task registry and delivery-policy code where the default resolver would live.
